attachments.origin_landmark: superficial head: flexor retinaculum; deep head: trapezium/capitate

functional_compartments.name: Superficial head
functional_compartments.function_note: Documented separately-innervated head -- median nerve, matching its embryological/functional grouping with the other thenar muscles.
functional_compartments.source: Holzbaur KR, Murray WM, Delp SL (2005) Ann Biomed Eng 33(6):829-840 -- upper-extremity muscle architecture model (fascicle length, pennation, PCSA)

relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.method: actual spindle count divided by the count predicted from muscle mass, by Banks' allometric correction
relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.notes: Comparable across muscles of different size because it is normalised by predicted count rather than by mass.
relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.source: Xie P, Jiang Y, Zhang X, Yang S, 'The Study of Intramuscular Nerve Distribution Patterns and Relative Spindle Abundance of the Thenar and Hypothenar Muscles in Human Hand', PLoS One 7(12):e51538 (2012), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0051538 -- 40 hands from 20 adult cadavers, modified Sihler's stain with haematoxylin-eosin spindle counts

motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler's stain intramuscular nerve mapping
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Minor branches densely distributed in the middle area of the head. The source states this in words rather than as a measured percentage -- it is a hand-surgery paper, not an injection-targeting one -- so the range is that wording read as thirds of muscle length, and nothing narrower is claimed.

functional_compartments.name: Deep head
functional_compartments.function_note: Deep head is classically described as ulnar-nerve innervated (superficial head median-nerve) -- the hand's parallel to adductor magnus's dual innervation in the thigh -- though cadaveric studies find this split considerably more variable in practice than the textbook model: the superficial head carries dual median+ulnar innervation in roughly 30% of specimens, and the deep head's innervation pattern (including occasional median-only supply) also varies (adjusted for this nuance after adversarial fact-check, see docs/VERIFICATION.md).

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Transverse on the palm over the thenar eminence, medial to abductor pollicis brevis and superficial to the first metacarpal cortex.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Thenar group; superficial and deep heads are separately resolvable, divided by an intramuscular fascia.
structures_at_risk: flexor pollicis longus tendon (a landmark, not a hazard)
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: A primary driver of the thumb-in-hand pattern in cerebral palsy, where it interferes with hygiene, risks skin breakdown and blocks grasp, pinch and release.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Diaconu S et al. (Elias University Hospital), 'A Visual Guide to Ultrasound-Guided Botulinum Toxin Injection in Spasticity: Part I -- Distal Upper Limb Muscles', Toxins 17(3):107 (2025), doi:10.3390/toxins17030107

relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.method: actual spindle count divided by the count predicted from muscle mass, by Banks' allometric correction
relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.notes: Extramuscular nerve trunk length 1.70 +/- 0.12 cm. Comparable across muscles of different size because it is normalised by predicted count rather than by mass.
relative_muscle_spindle_abundance.source: Xie P, Jiang Y, Zhang X, Yang S, 'The Study of Intramuscular Nerve Distribution Patterns and Relative Spindle Abundance of the Thenar and Hypothenar Muscles in Human Hand', PLoS One 7(12):e51538 (2012), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0051538 -- 40 hands from 20 adult cadavers, modified Sihler's stain with haematoxylin-eosin spindle counts

notes: A genuinely compartmented muscle, and this atlas's split into superficial and deep heads is confirmed by it: the superficial head is supplied by the recurrent branch of the MEDIAN nerve and the deep head by the deep branch of the ULNAR nerve, and each head has its own fibre direction, origin and insertion. The two are separable as independent flaps. For injection this means the two heads must be treated as two targets on two different nerves, not as one muscle.
